title: A required migration input has no immutable identity

scenario.observed_change: An architecture requires later implementation to incorporate statement-level requirements from external review-guidance documents, but those documents are not stored at an immutable repository path, pinned revision, digest, or embedded inventory. Different follow-up implementations can therefore select different document versions while claiming to implement the same accepted baseline.
controlled_inputs: version of the external guidance selected by a follow-up implementation
migration mapping from guidance statements into repository authority layers
authority_boundaries: historical design discussion versus repository-frozen migration input
explanatory reference to an external document versus reproducible normative migration baseline
operation_model: architecture names an external guidance artifact as required migration input
follow-up implementation later resolves whichever version is available or remembered
different implementations classify different statements into policy or procedure
the accepted semantic baseline changes without an explicit reviewed repository change

required_invariants.requirement: A statement used as a basis for review or policy migration must have determinable authority, current identity, and applicable scope rather than being selected from an ambiguous historical or explanatory source.

must_investigate: whether every required migration input has an immutable repository identity or frozen content inventory
whether follow-up implementations can select different versions without changing reviewed repository authority
whether the external guidance is evidence, explanation, or an actual migration baseline
must_identify: the required migration baseline is not reproducible because the referenced guidance has no immutable identity or frozen statement inventory
must_not_claim: deterministic migration merely because the architecture names the external guidance documents descriptively

provenance.note: The historical thread found that required review-guidance migration inputs were referenced without repository-frozen identities, allowing later work to silently choose different conversational/document variants. The thread evidence available through the current connector does not expose an exact reviewed-head binding for this comment.
